newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electricity ends lower on Intertie delay.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electricity ends lower on Intertie delay.

text.p: Most NYMEX electricity futures ended higher, but the August California-Oregon border (COB) contract fell in late trade on news that final okay to lift southbound capacity on the Pacific Intertie is unlikely before late next week, market sources said Friday.
"At the very end, August COB got hammered," said one dealer.
Early in the session, September contracts were boosted by heavy buying from one company, sources said.
Southwest prices were firm amid expectations for higher cooling demand, they noted.

But comments by the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) that an approved 600 megawatt (MW) rise in the Intertie's capacity will not be implemented until at least late next week sent a bearish signal for Northwest prices.
"There was not really that much actual trading, but the bids ran for the hills," said a trader.
The August COB contract settled 42 cents lower at $20.68 per megawatt hour (MWh), after trading as high as $21.20.
September COB closed 55 cents higher at $22.63 per MWh, while the October contract gained 30 cents to close at $21.50.
August Palo Verde (PV) rose $1.56 to settle at $37.05 per MWh, compared with an interday high of $37.25.
PV for September was up $1.27 at $29.97, while the October PV contract gained 60 cents to close at $23.60.
As of 1535 EDT, NYMEX estimated 1,226 PV and 382 COB contracts were sold.

The 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear complex near Phoenix, Arizona was set Sunday to begin slowly ramping down to between 60 and 80 percent power by September 6, when it was scheduled to shut for refueling.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, the National Weather Service expected above normal temperatures westward from Texas to the Pacific Ocean, except for near normal over northwestern Washington and much of the Central Valley in California.
Much above normal temperatures were forecast for most of the Dakotas, northwestern Nebraska, northern Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, northeastern Utah and southeastern Idaho.
